paragraphs: Hyman identifies him as Rabbi Meir’s father-in-law, as in Shabbat 147a: “R' Yehoshua ben Ziruz, the son of Rabbi Meir’s father-in-law.”[^1]

notes.text: The actual whole Davidson Shabbat 147a paragraph gives untitled Yehoshua ben Ziruz, son of Rabbi Meir’s father-in-law. The corresponding Meir title is locally supported; the source Yehoshua title remains R' in the new body. The father-in-law conclusion is explicitly Hyman’s interpretation of the chain, without a new genealogy binding.
